raw_response:
I am getting older, so I do not want to toss money around, but I also cannot let the crop go hungry. On my 10.1 mu, I will still do the wheat-maize rotation the same as before. That system is the steadiest for my family. I have only two people at home, so I want the management to be reliable and not too fussy. The extension people usually talk about more precise rates, but on my land I still judge by what I saw in past years: if the wheat seedlings come up even and stay dark green, I keep to the usual plan; if they look weak or yellow at jointing, I add a little topdressing. Water from the well helps, but pumping costs money, so I will irrigate at the key stages, not too many times.

For wheat, I will sow in early October with an improved local variety that people around here use a lot. I will put most fertilizer down as base fertilizer, then one topdress around jointing. Wheat is the main crop for a steady harvest, so I do not want to under-apply. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant maize right away within a few days. That turnaround is always tight, so I will keep tillage simple and use the machine or a quick shallow pass if available. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, give enough fertilizer for a decent ear, and watch summer rain before deciding on extra irrigation. Herbicide is necessary in both crops, and if insects show up in maize I will spray once. I am aiming for a stable yield, not the highest possible one.
